key_insight: LLM-generated world models can pass strict mechanical checks while still misrepresenting the structure of the intended decision problem.
engineering_relevance: Planning and verification pipelines should assess structural and semantic fidelity rather than treating executability as proof of correctness.
method: Benchmark five LLMs on 44 game, situational, and cultural scenarios.
Generate world models as partially observable stochastic games.
Evaluate mechanical validity, reference-relative structural agreement, and semantic criteria.
evidence_signal: Across 410 first-pass generations, the reference-backed game track achieved 134/135 mechanical passes, but mean structural F1 was 0.366 and only 28/134 valid models exactly matched the reference.
watch_item: Reference agreement is not definitive correctness when multiple formalizations are plausible, and automated semantic scores may miss consequential structural changes.
paper_title: Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
